info.title: TrueCalc Studio Cloud API
info.description:
The TrueCalc Studio command/query API. Every spreadsheet operation is a Command submitted to `POST /workbooks/{id}/commands`; the request body is a discriminated union over `type`, so one endpoint carries the whole write surface. Reads are their own `read:*` commands plus two GET routes.

This document is generated from the same schemas the server validates every request against, so it cannot drift from the implementation.

PRE-RELEASE: the API is not yet deployed and does not yet authenticate callers — see the security scheme. `POST /workbooks` is a convenience route for creating a workbook and is not part of the command contract proper.

post.description: A convenience route, not part of the core command contract: a real server's create flow is billing/entitlement-gated, out of scope for this mock. Ignores any request body; the created workbook always gets the mock defaults (1000 rows x 26 columns, one sheet named "Sheet1").

201.description: Workbook created — its identity and initial checkpoint version.

post.summary: Apply a batch of commands to a workbook
post.description: Validates the WHOLE batch (shape, capability, sheet, commandId reuse) before applying anything; a commandId already committed in a prior batch is recognized and its cached result replayed rather than re-applied, so retrying a batch with the same commandIds is safe. A per-command apply() failure is NOT a batch failure — it lands as an `ok: false` CommandResult with its own `error.code` (see CommandResult); the whole batch is still 200 unless the batch itself was rejected pre-apply (400) or an OCC precondition failed (409).

200.description: The batch was accepted (every command validated + dispatched); check each result's own `ok` for whether ITS apply succeeded.

get.description: Only the latest checkpoint is servable today (no history endpoint yet). No request headers are read by this route — neither `Authorization` nor any of the three contract headers; `security: []` reflects that faithfully rather than implying a check that does not exist.
A per-call agent read, answered from an in-memory cache of the workbook when resident. No request headers are read by this route — same `security: []` note as GET /workbooks/{id}.

200.description: The cell's raw formula, resolved value, display string, and format.

commandId.description: Client-minted idempotency key for this command, e.g. "cmd_a1B2c3D4". Generate a fresh one per command; resubmitting the same commandId is treated as a retry of the same operation, not a new one.

sheet.description: The target sheet within the workbook, e.g. "sh_a1B2c3D4". Obtained from the workbook document (its sheet list), not chosen freely by an agent.

from.description: An A1-style single-cell reference (column letters + a 1-based row), e.g. "B3".

to.description: An A1-style single-cell reference (column letters + a 1-based row), e.g. "B3".

range.description: Inclusive rectangle, e.g. { from: "A1", to: "B3" }. A single cell repeats from/to.

chartType.description: Which chart form to draw. An inapplicable form (e.g. scatter over a single numeric column) is REJECTED server-side with the reason, rather than inserted blank.

options.description: Renderer options, e.g. { orientation: 'rows' } to switch rows/columns, or { columnRoles: ['date','value'] } for a calendar heatmap / Sankey.

ChartInsert.description: Chart a range — creates a chart bound to those cells (a live reference, not a snapshot) and returns its chartId. Undoes in one step. Rejected with the reason if the range is a single cell, or if the chart form cannot render the data that is in the range RIGHT NOW (checked once, at insert time). column/bar/line/area are never rejected on shape — they accept any data, including an empty range, so with those you may insert first and fill the cells afterwards. Every other form needs its data in place first. Note: charts are reachable here regardless of the browser-side "Enable charts" preview toggle, which gates only the Insert menu item.

ClipboardPaste.description: Apply clipboard contents (an origin cell's raw input) at a target cell. cut: true moves it verbatim and clears source; cut: false (default) ref-adjusts formulas and leaves source untouched.

range.description: Restrict the search/replace to this range. Omit to search the WHOLE active sheet (every non-empty cell) — never inferred from a "current selection", since the wire has no such concept.

to.description: An A1-style single-cell reference (column letters + a 1-based row), e.g. "B3".

query.description: The text (or, when useRegex is true, pattern) to find.

replacement.description: The replacement text. May be empty, which removes every match.

matchCase.description: Case-sensitive comparison. Sheets' default is case-INsensitive (false).

useRegex.description: Treat query as a JavaScript RegExp pattern (an accepted divergence from Sheets' own RE2 engine). An invalid pattern matches nothing rather than erroring.

matchEntireCell.description: Only count a cell whose ENTIRE search text equals query as a match.

withinFormulas.description: When false (default), a formula cell is matched by its computed DISPLAY value and is never replaced (only found/counted) — never silently rewriting a formula's semantics from a value-level text match. When true, a formula cell is matched AND replaced by its RAW FORMULA TEXT instead, Sheets' "Also search within formulas".

EditFindReplace.description: Replace every occurrence of query with replacement across a range (or the whole active sheet) — the wire equivalent of Find and replace's "Replace all", applied as ONE undoable command.

source.description: The seed range the fill-handle drag STARTS from — its cells are read (never rewritten) to detect the series.

to.description: The cell the drag ENDS at (the fill handle's final position), e.g. "A10". Extends down when below source's bottom edge, right when past its right edge; any other position is a well-defined no-op (nothing to fill).

EditAutofill.description: Extend source into a series (drag-the-fill-handle behavior): numeric/date trends extrapolate, recognized weekday/month names advance, everything else repeats — the same detection Sheets' own fill handle performs. Applied as ONE undoable command.

data.description: The canonical-JSON workbook payload as a string — the same shape produced by file:export with format:"json". A malformed payload is rejected with a descriptive parse error. A valid payload is loaded for real: every sheet is created as a NEW sheet on this workbook (never replacing/overwriting an existing sheet) and filled with the FULL document graph the payload carries — cells, formats, column/row size overrides, frozen panes, the single-column filter, merged ranges, charts, conditional-format rules, banded ranges, data-validation rules, and page setup. Chart/conditional-format/banded-range/validation-rule ids are preserved verbatim from the payload (never re-minted). Workbook-scoped named ranges are also restored, retargeted to whatever (possibly deduped, e.g. "Sheet1 (2)") name each sheet actually lands on — a named range whose NAME collides with one already defined in this workbook, OR with any sheet name (existing or newly imported), is skipped (the existing binding, or the sheet, wins), not overwritten and not a fatal error. A file:export -> file:import round trip therefore preserves the full document graph.

FileImport.description: Load a canonical-JSON workbook payload (the same shape file:export produces) as one or more NEW sheets appended to this workbook, restoring the full document graph: cells, formats, size overrides, frozen panes, filter, merges, charts, conditional formats, banded ranges, validation rules, page setup, and named ranges (retargeted to the actual imported sheet names).

SheetAdd.description: Create a new sheet, appended as the last tab and made active. Returns the newly minted sheetId — usable by a FOLLOW-UP command/batch, not the one that created it.

sheet.description: The sheet to delete.

SheetDelete.description: Delete a sheet. Dependent formulas on OTHER sheets are NOT rewritten — their text is preserved verbatim and they evaluate to #REF! until the sheet is restored (e.g. by undo) or re-created under the same name. Refuses to delete the workbook's only sheet. No reference-count warning is returned (Google Sheets does not detect dependents at delete time either).

commandId.description: Client-minted idempotency key for this command, e.g. "cmd_a1B2c3D4". Generate a fresh one per command; resubmitting the same commandId is treated as a retry of the same operation, not a new one.

sheet.description: The sheet to rename.

name.description: The new name for the sheet. Must not collide, case-insensitively, with any other sheet on this workbook — a colliding name is REFUSED with a clean error, not deduplicated (unlike file:import, which resolves a colliding imported name via " (2)", " (3)", …; sheet:rename never does).

SheetRename.description: Rename a sheet. Google Sheets REWRITES every dependent formula's TEXT to the new name (e.g. =OldName!A1*2 becomes =NewName!A1*2, value unchanged) — the exact opposite of sheet:delete, which preserves a referencing formula's text verbatim and lets it evaluate to #REF!. A colliding name (case-insensitive) is refused with a clean error; the rename does not happen.

commandId.description: Client-minted idempotency key for this command, e.g. "cmd_a1B2c3D4". Generate a fresh one per command; resubmitting the same commandId is treated as a retry of the same operation, not a new one.

sheet.description: The sheet to move.

direction.description: Move the sheet one position toward the start ("left") or end ("right") of the tab order. A no-op when the sheet is already at that end — moving right from the rightmost tab, or left from the leftmost, changes nothing, matching Google Sheets' own bounds-aware "Move right"/"Move left" tab-menu items.

SheetReorder.description: Move a sheet one tab position left or right. Presentation only — no formula or computed value is affected (the engine addresses sheets by name, not position). Bounds-aware: a no-op at either end of the tab order.

SheetSetActive.description: Make sheet the active (current) sheet on this workbook — the tab GET /workbooks reports as sheetId/sheetName. A pure view change (matches a tab-bar click); no cell content is touched, and it is not undoable.

code.description: A stable, machine-readable failure reason for a single command in the batch. Two codes are produced today: "not_implemented" for a command whose operation is documented as not yet supported (no command currently reports this), and "apply_failed" for any other runtime failure — a malformed payload that passed schema validation, an out-of-range write, or a refused operation. Deliberately not an `enum`: a future command may introduce its own code, and a client should treat an unrecognised value as a generic failure rather than rejecting the response.

CheckpointVersionQuery.name: version
CheckpointVersionQuery.description: Only the LATEST checkpoint is servable (no history) — a value that does not match the current version returns a clean 404, never a silent fall-through to HEAD.

IfMatchHeader.name: If-Match
IfMatchHeader.description: Optimistic-concurrency precondition — the VersionId this batch's caller last read as HEAD. Enforced ONLY when the resolved X-Studio-Api-Version declares the "command_batch_occ" capability AND the batch contains at least one mutating command (a batch containing ONLY read:* commands — getRange, getFormats, getSheets, etc. — is exempt, matched by the "read:" prefix); on an incapable or unrecognized API version this header is silently ignored and the write proceeds unconditionally. A stale or missing token on an enforcing version returns 409 version_conflict, echoing both the token the caller sent and the actual current version.

ApiVersionHeader.name: X-Studio-Api-Version
ApiVersionHeader.description: Selects which behavioral capabilities this request gets — dated version strings, looked up in a plain registry, never regex-parsed. An unrecognized or missing value resolves to "no capabilities", identically. Only "2026-07-17.preview" is registered today, and is exactly what a missing header resolves to (DEFAULT_VERSION).

StudioChannelHeader.name: X-Studio-Channel
StudioChannelHeader.description: Declares the calling surface, recorded as per-commit attribution in the checkpoint history. An unrecognized or missing value defaults to "api".

InvalidRequest.description: The batch was rejected before anything was applied: malformed shape, an unrecognized command type, a schema-shape violation, a command whose type requires a capability the resolved API version lacks, an unknown `sheet`, or a `commandId` reused across commits with a different payload.

NotFound.description: No such workbook, no such cell (out of the sheet's declared extent), or (GET /workbooks/{id}?version=) a requested checkpoint version other than the current HEAD.

VersionConflict.description: `If-Match` did not match the current HEAD version, on an API version that enforces the "command_batch_occ" capability.

bearerAuth.description: PRE-RELEASE: this API does not yet authenticate callers. The bearer token is read but never verified — an "ak_"-prefixed value is attributed to an API-key actor and anything else, including an absent or empty header, to a generic user actor. Any string, or none at all, is accepted. Attribution only, not authentication: do not expose this surface to untrusted callers until key issuance ships.
